missing_data: How buyers place Lay's against 'better-for-you' brands — no survey or panel data was collected.
Sales by product line, to see whether the natural cue moved purchases in either direction.
Who the commenters are (age, purchase frequency) — profiles are removed by design, so the audience split cannot be confirmed.
Any reaction from the ~42% the research said the message was built for.

hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rejected on counter-evidence, not for lack of it: design press and commenters find the pack still distinct and identifiable (ev_007, ev_037, ev_003). The confusion people report is with Lay's own Baked line, which belongs to H5, not with competitors.

missing_data: Whether the claim changed purchase intent — no survey or sales data.
A shelf test of how quickly shoppers tell Classic from Baked — the confusion is reported, not measured.
Competitor share, pricing or launch activity in the same period — not collected.
hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rejected on counter-evidence: the context people bring up is Lay's own — smaller bags and earlier pack-size cuts (ev_031, ev_062) — and category data shows Lay's still growing (ev_064). No item points to a rival's launch or message.

uncertainty_reasons: The sample is self-selected and Reddit-heavy (34 of 65 items); people who comment are not all buyers.
Some taste complaints may reflect the real recipe change rather than the pack (ev_017).
